title: Phrasal verbs frecuentes
short: Verbo + partícula = significado nuevo: look (mirar) → look ==for== (buscar), look ==after== (cuidar). Turn ==it on==, nunca «turn on it».

story.title: Un verbo con apellido
story.text: Un ==phrasal verb== es un verbo + una partícula (up, on, off, for…). Juntos significan ==otra cosa==, a veces muy distinta.

story.title: Los más útiles
story.text: Apréndelos como un bloque, con su ejemplo.

head: Phrasal verb
Significa
Ejemplo
rows: I'll pick you up at six.

story.title: Los que se separan
story.text: Con turn on, put on, pick up, take off… el objeto puede ir en medio. Con un ==pronombre==, ==siempre en medio==: turn ==it== on.

examples.t: Turn off the light. / Turn the light off.

story.title: Los que no se separan
story.text: Con look for, look after, get on with… la partícula va ==pegada al verbo== y el pronombre, ==detrás==.

examples.t: I look after them on Mondays.

story.title: En español, un solo verbo
story.text: Nosotras decimos «buscar», «apagar», «recoger». En inglés el significado está en el ==bloque entero==: no traduzcas palabra por palabra.

story.title: Errores típicos
story.text:
❌ Turn on it. ✅ Turn ==it on==.
❌ I'm looking after my keys. ✅ I'm looking ==for== my keys.
❌ Pick up me at six. ✅ Pick ==me up== at six.

story.title: Acento en la partícula
story.text: Al hablar, la fuerza suele ir en la ==partícula==: give ==UP==, pick it ==UP==, turn it ==OFF==. Así te entienden mejor.

compare.es: En español usamos un verbo propio para cada idea: buscar, cuidar, apagar, recoger, enterarse, levantarse, dejar de.
compare.target: En inglés muchas de esas ideas se dicen con un verbo corriente + partícula (look for, look after, turn off, pick up, find out, get up, give up). Hay que aprenderlos como un bloque. Con los separables, el pronombre va en medio (turn it off, pick me up); con los no separables, detrás (look for it, look after them).

errors.wrong: Can you turn on it, please?
errors.right: Can you turn it on, please?
errors.why: Con un pronombre, va en medio: turn it on.
Buscar = look for. Look after = cuidar.

errors.wrong: Pick up me at the station.
errors.right: Pick me up at the station.
errors.why: El pronombre me va entre pick y up.

errors.wrong: Put off your coat, it's cold.
errors.right: Put on your coat, it's cold.
errors.why: Ponerse ropa = put on. Put off significa aplazar.

errors.wrong: I look after it them every day.
errors.right: I look after them every day.
errors.why: Un solo pronombre, detrás de look after.

exercises.q: I usually ___ at seven o'clock.
I'm looking ___ my glasses. Have you seen them?
I ___ my grandson on Tuesdays.
My husband ___ smoking ten years ago.
exercises.why: Dejar un hábito = give up (pasado gave up).

exercises.q: It's dark in here. Can you ___ the light?
I'll pick ___ at the station.
exercises.why: El pronombre va en medio: pick you up.

exercises.q: Your plants? Don't worry, I'll look ___.
exercises.why: Look after no se separa: look after them.

exercises.q: We ___ at six to catch the early train.
Oh no! We've ___ milk.
exercises.why: Quedarse sin algo = run out of + cosa.

exercises.q: Put ___ your coat; it's cold outside.
exercises.es: Ponte el abrigo; hace frío fuera.

exercises.q: Please take ___ your shoes before you come in.
exercises.es: Por favor, quítate los zapatos antes de entrar.

exercises.q: I need to find ___ what time the train leaves.
exercises.es: Tengo que averiguar a qué hora sale el tren.

exercises.q: Can you call me ___ later? I'm driving.
exercises.es: ¿Me puedes volver a llamar luego? Estoy conduciendo.

exercises.q: I'm really looking ___ to seeing you.
exercises.why: Tener ganas de = look forward to.

exercises.q: Turn ___ the oven; the cake is ready.
exercises.es: Apaga el horno; la tarta está lista.

exercises.q: My grandson gets ___ really well with his cousins.
exercises.es: Mi nieto se lleva muy bien con sus primos.
exercises.why: Llevarse bien con = get on well with.

exercises.q: Turn off the radio.
exercises.why: Con pronombre, en medio: turn it off.

exercises.q: I picked up the children at five.
answer: I picked them up at five.
exercises.why: Pick up se separa: picked them up.

exercises.q: I'll look after my grandson.
exercises.why: Look after no se separa: look after him.

exercises.q: Put on your jacket.
exercises.why: Put on es separable: put your jacket on.

exercises.q: I'm looking after my keys. Where are they?
exercises.why: Buscar = look for. Look after = cuidar.

exercises.q: She gave down smoking last year.
I get on at seven every morning.
exercises.why: Levantarse = get up. Get on es subir (al autobús) o llevarse bien.

exercises.q: Put off your coat, it's freezing.
exercises.why: Ponerse = put on. Put off es aplazar.

exercises.q: We've run up of sugar.

exercises.es: Cuido de mi nieto los lunes
exercises.answer: I look after my grandson on Mondays
I'll pick you up at the station

exercises.q: Mi marido dejó de fumar.
answer: My husband has given up smoking.

exercises.q: Me levanto a las siete.
answer: I get up at seven o'clock.

exercises.q: I found out that she was pregnant.
answer: Me enteré de que estaba embarazada.
